## Shopify SEO: what to fix first
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/shopify-seo/

Q: What does a Shopify SEO expert do?
A: A Shopify SEO expert makes a Shopify store rank for the searches its buyers use: collection pages that target category searches, unique product pages, clean canonicals for Shopify's duplicate product URLs, a fast theme, product schema for rich results and buying guides that earn links, measured in organic orders. RankEmpire's ecommerce plans start at $799 a month, month to month after onboarding.

Shopify gives stores a solid base, but a few platform habits hold most stores back. This is the order we fix them in.

### Make collection pages worth ranking
Collections usually match the searches with the most buyers, such as "men's trail running shoes". Add a short, useful introduction, clear filters and FAQs, and link related collections. A collection with no text rarely beats a marketplace.

### Fix Shopify's duplicate product URLs
Shopify links to products through /collections/name/products/ paths as well as /products/. Make sure internal links point to the canonical /products/ URL and that tag and filter pages do not flood the index. Our technical SEO basics (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/technical-seo-basics/) guide explains canonicals and indexing.

### Write product pages for buyers, not suppliers
Replace manufacturer copy on the products that sell with unique descriptions, real photos, sizing and shipping answers. Product schema with price, stock and reviews helps earn rich results.

### Speed: fewer apps, lighter theme
Every app can add scripts to every page. Remove the ones you do not use, compress images and test on mobile. Faster stores rank and convert better.

### Measure organic revenue
Track orders from organic search in Shopify and GA4, not just rankings. See how to tell if your SEO is working (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-tell-if-seo-is-working/), our ecommerce SEO services (https://www.rankempire.us/ecommerce-seo/) and how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/).

## Local citations: what to fix first
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/local-citation-building/

Q: What is local citation building?
A: Local citation building lists your business name, address and phone number consistently on the directories, maps and data aggregators that Google, Apple, Bing and AI assistants check, and fixes wrong or duplicate listings. Accurate citations support map pack rankings and correct answers about your business. RankEmpire includes citation building and cleanup in local SEO plans from $599 a month.

Citation work pays off when it is done in the right order. This is the order we use for every local business.

### Agree one exact version of your details
Pick one business name, address format and phone number, matching your website and Google Business Profile, and use it everywhere. Small differences such as Suite vs Ste matter less than wrong numbers or old addresses.

### Fix the core platforms first
Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, Yelp, Facebook and the BBB are seen by the most customers and checked most by search engines and AI assistants. Our Google Business Profile checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) covers the most important one.

### Remove duplicates
Duplicate listings split reviews and confuse search engines. Search each platform for your old addresses and phone numbers, and merge or remove what you find.

### Add industry and city directories
After the core, add the directories for your trade and your city, such as professional associations and the local chamber. These are worth more than hundreds of generic sites.

### Citations are one part of local SEO
Citations support rankings, but reviews, service pages and the profile itself do most of the work. See our local SEO checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-checklist/), the 90-day local SEO roadmap (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/) and our local SEO services (https://www.rankempire.us/local-seo/).

# Blog posts

## How to Tell If Your SEO Is Working (and If Your SEO Company Is)
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-tell-if-seo-is-working/
Updated: 2026-11-18

SEO is working when the right searches show your site more often, your positions for those searches improve, and that visibility turns into calls, forms and sales, in that order. Because each step lags the one before it, many business owners judge SEO too early or by the wrong number. This guide shows how to check whether your SEO, or your SEO company, is working, what to look at in each month, and the signs that something is genuinely wrong.

### The order SEO results arrive in

SEO results show up in a predictable sequence. Knowing it is the easiest way to tell slow progress from no progress:

| Stage | What changes | Where to see it | Typical timing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Indexing | Pages are crawled and indexed | Search Console, Pages report | Days to weeks |
| 2. Impressions | Your pages appear for more searches | Search Console, Performance | Weeks 2 to 8 |
| 3. Positions | Average position improves for target queries | Search Console, Queries tab | Months 2 to 6 |
| 4. Clicks | Visits from search grow | Search Console and analytics | Once pages reach page one |
| 5. Leads | Calls, forms and bookings from organic visits | Call tracking, form and analytics events | Follows clicks |

Clicks stay low until pages reach the first page of Google, because almost nobody clicks results on page five. That is why impressions and positions are the early signals to watch.

### A real example: our own first weeks

RankEmpire's own site shows this sequence clearly. In Google Search Console, daily impressions grew from about 970 on 29 October 2026 to about 3,200 on 15 November 2026, and the daily average position improved from about 85 to about 81. Clicks over the same period stayed in single digits, because most pages still ranked beyond the first page. At that stage SEO is working in the sense that Google is showing the site for more searches and ranking it a little higher each week, but it has not yet reached the point where it produces traffic. Judging it by clicks alone would have suggested nothing was happening.

### How to check if your SEO is working in Search Console

1. **Open Performance, then Search results.** Set the date range to the last three months and compare with the previous period.
2. **Check total impressions.** A steady rise means Google is showing your site for more searches.
3. **Open the Queries tab.** Find the searches that matter to your business, such as your services and your city, and note their average position over time.
4. **Open the Pages tab.** Check that your service and location pages, not only the home page, are gaining impressions.
5. **Check the Pages report under Indexing.** Important pages should be indexed; "Discovered, currently not indexed" on key pages is a problem to fix.
6. **Match clicks to leads.** In your analytics, count calls, forms and bookings that came from organic search.

You can also spot-check positions with our free keyword rank checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/).

### Signs your SEO is working

- Impressions rise month over month for searches related to your services.
- Average position improves for your target keywords, even if they are not on page one yet.
- New pages get indexed within days or weeks.
- More of your pages, not just the home page, appear in search results.
- Your Google Business Profile shows more searches, calls and direction requests.
- Organic leads grow once key pages reach the first page.

### Signs your SEO is not working

Give a campaign three to four months before judging rankings, but these warning signs are worth raising at any time:

- **Impressions are flat or falling** after two to three months of work.
- **Important pages are not indexed,** or keep dropping out of the index.
- **Reports show activity, not outcomes:** lists of tasks and "links built" with no Search Console data.
- **Rankings are reported only for keywords nobody searches** or for your brand name.
- **Your agency cannot explain** what they changed and why a metric moved.
- **Traffic grows but leads do not,** which usually means the wrong searches or pages that do not convert.

Our guide on why most SEO campaigns fail (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/why-most-seo-campaigns-fail/) explains the usual causes behind these signs.

### How to tell if your SEO company is working

Ask your SEO company for these every month. A good one will provide them without being asked:

- Search Console impressions, clicks and average position, compared with the previous period
- Positions for an agreed list of target keywords
- Pages created or improved, and what changed on each
- Indexing status of new and important pages
- Organic leads: calls, forms and bookings
- The plan for next month and why

If a report contains none of these, ask for access to your own Search Console and analytics. You should always own those accounts.

### What to do if your SEO is not working

1. **Check the foundations.** Make sure key pages are indexed, load quickly on mobile and each target one clear search.
2. **Check intent.** If the wrong searches bring visitors, retarget pages to the searches your customers make.
3. **Check authority.** If pages are well built but stuck beyond page three, the site likely needs real links and mentions from relevant sites; buying cheap link packages usually makes this worse.
4. **Check your Google Business Profile** if you depend on local searches.
5. **Get a second opinion.** An independent SEO audit (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-audit/) shows what is holding the site back.

### How long before SEO should work?

Most sites see impressions rise within the first two months, meaningful position gains for target searches within four to six months, and lead growth after that. Low-competition and local searches move faster; competitive national terms take longer. See how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) for what to expect at each budget.

### Sources

- Google Search Central: Do you need an SEO? (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo)

### FAQ

#### How do I know if my SEO is working?

Check Google Search Console. If impressions are rising, average positions for your target searches are improving and important pages are indexed, SEO is working. Clicks and leads follow once pages reach the first page of results.

#### How do I tell if my SEO company is working?

Ask for monthly Search Console data, positions for agreed target keywords, a list of pages changed and organic leads. If your company reports only tasks completed or links built, without this data, it is hard to know whether the work is paying off.

#### Does SEO really work?

Yes, for businesses whose customers search for what they sell, but it takes months and depends on the site's technical health, content and authority. It does not work when nobody searches for the service or when shortcuts such as bought links are used.

#### Why is my SEO not working?

The most common reasons are pages that are not indexed, content that does not match what people search for, one page targeting too many topics, low authority from few real links, and judging results too early.

#### How long does it take to see SEO results?

Impressions usually rise within weeks, positions improve over two to six months, and clicks and leads grow once pages reach the first page. Competitive searches take longer.

#### How do I track SEO results?

Use Google Search Console for impressions, clicks, positions and indexing, analytics for organic visits and leads, and call tracking or form events for conversions. Compare month over month rather than day to day.


## Who Is the Best Local SEO Company? How to Tell Before You Hire
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/who-is-the-best-local-seo-company/
Updated: 2026-11-17

There is no single best local SEO company for every business. Google does not rank, certify or endorse SEO companies, and the agencies at the top of "best of" lists are often there because of reviews, paid placements or their own marketing. The best local SEO company for you is the one that can prove results in markets like yours, shows you real Search Console data, explains its plan in plain language and charges a fair, published price. This guide explains how to tell, step by step.

### Is there an official "best local SEO company"?

For a worked example, see how we answer best SEO company near me in Chicago (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/chicago/) and what to ask SEO experts near me in Houston (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/houston/).

No. Three things are often mistaken for an official ranking:

- **Google.** Google does not rank or recommend SEO agencies. Its Search Central documentation explains what a good SEO should do and warns against anyone who guarantees rankings, but it does not name companies. Google Partners is a program for Google Ads, not for SEO.
- **Agency directories.** Sites such as Clutch, UpCity, DesignRush and Expertise rank agencies using reviews, project details and their own criteria, and some offer sponsored placement. They are useful for finding candidates and reading verified reviews, but a top spot is not proof of results for your type of business.
- **"Best SEO companies" articles.** Many are written by agencies ranking themselves first, or by publishers paid per lead. Read them as a list of names to check, not as a verdict.

### What makes a local SEO company good

Local SEO is its own discipline. It is mostly decided in the Google Maps results, so the company you hire should be strong in the things that move the map pack:

1. **Google Business Profile work.** Categories, services, service areas, photos, posts and reviews. Ask how they choose the primary category and how they measure map visibility. Our Google Business Profile checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) shows what complete work looks like.
2. **Rank grids, not one ranking.** Map results change every few blocks. A good local SEO company measures your visibility across a grid of points in your service area, not with one keyword checked from its own office.
3. **Pages for each service and area.** One strong page per service and real service area pages where you work, not hundreds of near-identical city pages.
4. **A review system.** A simple process that asks every customer for a review that mentions the job and the town.
5. **Reporting from your own data.** Search Console, Google Business Profile insights, calls and form leads, shared with you every month.

### How to check a local SEO company before you hire

| Check | What to ask for | Good sign | Warning sign |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proof | Search Console or Business Profile results for a similar business | Screenshots with dates and context, shared with permission | Only ranking screenshots for unrelated keywords |
| People | Who will work on your account | A named strategist you can talk to | Account manager only, work outsourced |
| Plan | What happens in the first 90 days | A written plan in order of impact | "Proprietary system", no detail |
| Price | Monthly fee and what it includes | Published pricing, month-to-month after onboarding | 12-month lock-in, vague deliverables |
| Ownership | Who owns the profile, site and accounts | You own everything | Agency keeps logins or the profile |
| Promises | Expected timeline | Ranges and leading indicators | Guaranteed number one rankings |

Our longer guide on how to choose an SEO company (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/) lists twelve questions to ask in interviews.

### Who is the best local SEO company near me?

When you search for a local SEO company near you, Google shows agencies close to your location, but proximity matters less than whether the team understands your market. A remote company can rank you in your city if it measures visibility from your customers' locations and knows your industry's searches. If you prefer a local partner, check that their own Google Business Profile has recent, detailed reviews from businesses like yours. We work with businesses in cities across the US from our locations (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/) pages, and every plan starts with a free audit of your local competition.

### Which types of businesses need local SEO most?

Local SEO pays off fastest for businesses where customers search, call and buy nearby:

- **Home services:** plumbers, HVAC, electricians, roofers and other trades, where most jobs start with a map search. See SEO for contractors (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/seo-for-contractors/).
- **Health and wellness:** dentists, chiropractors, med spas and clinics, where patients compare reviews before booking.
- **Legal and professional services:** law firms, accountants and financial advisors.
- **Hospitality and retail:** restaurants, cafes, salons and gyms that depend on near-me searches.

National online businesses benefit more from content and technical SEO than from the map pack; for those, see national SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/national-seo/).

### How much a good local SEO company costs

Most single-location businesses pay roughly $500 to $2,500 a month for ongoing local SEO, with competitive metros and multi-location businesses at the higher end. RankEmpire publishes its prices: local plans start at $599 a month, with no long contracts. See how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) and our local SEO packages (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/local-seo/).


### Sources

- Google Search Central: Do you need an SEO? (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo)
- Google Business Profile Help: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google (https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en)

### FAQ

#### Who is the best local SEO company?

No company is the best for every business. The best local SEO company for you is one that can show Search Console and Google Business Profile results for similar businesses, measures map visibility with rank grids, gives you a written plan and publishes fair pricing without long contracts.

#### Who is Google's best local SEO company?

Google does not recommend or certify SEO companies. The Google Partners badge applies to Google Ads, not to SEO. Any agency claiming to be Google's preferred SEO company is misleading you.

#### Who is the best local SEO company in the nation?

There is no independent national ranking based on client results. Directories and "best of" lists combine reviews, self-reported data and sometimes paid placement. Use them to build a shortlist, then judge each company on proof, people, plan, price and ownership.

#### How do I find the best local SEO company near me?

Shortlist three to five companies from directories, referrals and your own searches, ask each for results from businesses like yours, a 90-day plan and pricing, and compare them side by side using the table above.

#### What type of company needs SEO the most?

Businesses whose customers search before they buy and choose a provider nearby: home services, medical and dental practices, law firms, restaurants, salons and other local services. For them, appearing in the map pack directly drives calls and bookings.


## Who Is the Best SEO Company in the USA? How to Choose the Right One
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/best-seo-company-in-the-usa/
Updated: 2026-11-17

Who is the best SEO company in the USA? The honest answer is that it depends on what you need. There are thousands of SEO agencies in the United States, from global firms with hundreds of staff to specialist teams that focus on one industry or one type of search. No independent body ranks them on results, and Google does not endorse any SEO company. This guide explains how the main types of SEO companies differ, how to judge "best SEO company" claims, and how to pick the right one for your business.

### Why there is no single best SEO company

If you need local results, compare our SEO services in the USA by city (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/) and our SEO company in Phoenix (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/phoenix/).

"Best" depends on the job. A national ecommerce brand, a SaaS company and a plumber in Phoenix need very different work:

| Your business | What the best SEO company for you does well |
| --- | --- |
| Local service business | Google Business Profile, map rankings, reviews, service and area pages |
| Multi-location brand | Location pages at scale, profile management, local reporting per location |
| Ecommerce store | Category and product pages, technical SEO, crawl budget, structured data |
| SaaS or B2B company | Content strategy, comparison and use-case pages, links, long sales cycles |
| Enterprise website | Technical SEO at scale, governance, migrations, international setups |

An agency that is excellent at one of these can be average at another. That is why the best SEO company in the USA for a law firm is rarely the best one for an online store.

### How to judge "best SEO company" lists

Search for the best SEO company in the US and you will find rankings from directories, publishers and agencies themselves. Before trusting one, check:

- **Who wrote it.** Lists published by an agency that ranks itself first are marketing.
- **How companies were chosen.** Some directories use verified client reviews; others also sell sponsored positions. Look for a methodology.
- **Whether results are shown.** Awards and badges are not the same as traffic and leads for clients like you.

Directories are still a good place to read verified reviews and build a shortlist. The decision should come from your own comparison.

### What the best SEO companies have in common

Whatever their size, strong SEO companies share a few habits:

1. **They show real data.** Results from Google Search Console and analytics, shared with client permission, not only ranking screenshots.
2. **They explain the plan.** A written roadmap for the first 90 days in order of impact, as in our 90-day local SEO roadmap (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/).
3. **A named person does the work.** You know who your strategist is and can talk to them.
4. **They do not guarantee rankings.** Google's own guidance warns against anyone who does.
5. **They price clearly.** Published or clearly itemized pricing and no long lock-in.
6. **You own everything.** Your website, Google Business Profile, Search Console and analytics stay in your name.

### Big agency, specialist or consultant?

- **Large national agencies** suit enterprise brands that need many disciplines and large teams. Expect higher minimum budgets and more layers between you and the people doing the work.
- **Specialist SEO companies** focus on a type of search, such as local, ecommerce or SaaS, or on specific industries. They often move faster for businesses in their niche. RankEmpire is a specialist in local and service-business SEO.
- **SEO consultants** advise and set strategy while your team implements. See SEO consulting (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-consulting/).

For a fuller explanation of the roles, read what an SEO company does (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/what-does-an-seo-company-do/).

### How to find the best SEO company for you

1. **Write down your goal.** More calls in one city, online sales, demo requests or national visibility.
2. **Shortlist three to five companies** that work with businesses like yours, from referrals, directories and search.
3. **Ask the same questions to each.** Use the twelve questions in our guide on how to choose an SEO company (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/).
4. **Compare proposals side by side:** proof, people, plan, price and ownership.
5. **Start with an audit.** A good company will show you what is holding your site back before asking for a long commitment. Ours is free: request an SEO audit (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-audit/).

### What SEO in the USA costs

Most small businesses pay about $500 to $2,500 a month; multi-location, ecommerce and national programs usually cost more. See how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) for a full breakdown and our SEO packages (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/) for RankEmpire's published prices, starting at $599 a month.


### Sources

- Google Search Central: Do you need an SEO? (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo)

### FAQ

#### Who is the best SEO company in the USA?

There is no independent ranking of SEO companies by client results, and Google does not endorse any agency. The best SEO company for you is one with proven results for businesses like yours, a clear plan, a named strategist, published pricing and no ranking guarantees.

#### What is the best SEO company for a small business?

Usually a specialist in local or small-business SEO that publishes its prices, works month to month after onboarding and focuses on the Google Business Profile, service pages and reviews. Large enterprise agencies are rarely the best value for small budgets.

#### How do I find the best SEO company?

Shortlist three to five companies that work in your industry, ask each for Search Console results from similar clients, a 90-day plan and pricing, and compare them side by side. Avoid any company that guarantees rankings.

#### Are "best SEO company" rankings reliable?

Use them as a starting point only. Some are based on verified reviews, some include paid placements, and some are published by agencies ranking themselves first. Check the methodology and then judge each company on its own evidence.

#### Does Google recommend SEO companies?

No. Google publishes guidance on what to expect from an SEO and what to avoid, but it does not recommend, certify or partner with SEO agencies. Google Partners applies to Google Ads only.


## What Does an SEO Company Do? SEO Services Explained (and When You Need One)
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/what-does-an-seo-company-do/
Updated: 2026-11-17

An SEO company improves how often a business appears in Google, Bing and AI answers for the searches its customers make, and turns that visibility into calls, bookings and sales. In practice that means fixing the website's technical health, writing and improving the pages that answer customer searches, optimizing the Google Business Profile, earning reviews and links, and reporting results from real data. This guide explains what SEO services include, how an SEO agency differs from a consultant, and how to tell whether you need one.

### What SEO services include

Most SEO work falls into six areas. A good SEO company covers all of them, in the order that matters most for your business.

| Area | What it involves | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Technical SEO | Crawling, indexing, site speed, mobile layout, structured data, redirects | Google cannot rank pages it cannot crawl, render or trust |
| On-page SEO | Titles, headings, internal links, matching each page to one search intent | Tells Google exactly which search a page answers |
| Content | Service pages, location pages, guides and FAQs | Creates pages for the searches customers actually make |
| Local SEO | Google Business Profile, reviews, citations, service areas | Decides who appears in the map pack for "near me" searches |
| Off-page SEO | Earning links and mentions from relevant sites | Builds the authority needed for competitive terms |
| Reporting | Search Console, analytics, calls and form leads | Shows whether the work is producing customers |

Each area has its own page if you want the detail: technical SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/technical-seo/), on-page SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/on-page-seo/), content SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/content-seo/), local SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/local-seo/) and link building (https://www.rankempire.us/link-building/).

### What an SEO company does in the first 90 days

The first three months set the direction. A typical sequence:

1. **Audit and baseline (weeks 1 to 2).** Crawl the site, check indexing in Google Search Console, review the Google Business Profile, compare competitors and record current impressions, clicks and leads.
2. **Fix what blocks rankings (weeks 2 to 6).** Indexing problems, broken pages, slow templates, missing titles, duplicate content and incorrect structured data.
3. **Build and improve pages (weeks 4 to 12).** One page per service, pages for the areas you really serve, and answers to the questions customers ask.
4. **Local and off-site work (ongoing).** Profile updates, a review request process, citations and the first earned links.
5. **Report and adjust (monthly).** Which searches gained impressions, which pages moved, and what changes next month.

Our 90-day local SEO roadmap (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/) shows this plan in more detail, with real data.

### SEO agency vs SEO consultant vs SEO company

The terms overlap, and the label matters less than who does the work.

- **SEO agency or SEO company:** a team that covers strategy, technical work, content and links. Best when you want the work done for you across several areas.
- **SEO consultant:** usually one specialist who advises, audits and sets strategy, while your team or another provider implements. Best when you have in-house people who can execute. See SEO consulting (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-consulting/).
- **Freelancer:** an individual who does a defined part of the work, such as content or technical fixes, often for a lower fee.

Whichever you choose, ask who will actually run your account and whether that person has experience in your industry.

### What an SEO company should not do

Some practices are red flags, whatever the price:

- **Guaranteeing rankings.** Nobody controls Google's results. Promises of "page one in 30 days" usually mean shortcuts.
- **Buying links in bulk.** Cheap link packages can lead to ranking losses that take months to recover.
- **Reporting only rankings.** Rankings without impressions, clicks and leads hide whether the work is paying off.
- **Locking you into long contracts.** A short onboarding period is reasonable; a 12-month lock-in is not.
- **Keeping your accounts.** Your Google Business Profile, Search Console and analytics should stay in your name.

Our guide on how to choose an SEO company (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/) lists 12 questions to ask before you sign, and how to tell if your SEO is working (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-tell-if-seo-is-working/) shows how to judge the results once you have.

### Do I need an SEO company?

You probably benefit from one if most of these are true:

- Customers find businesses like yours on Google or in Google Maps.
- Competitors appear above you for your main services in your area.
- Your site gets few calls or form leads from search, or you do not know how many it gets.
- Nobody on your team has several hours a week to work on SEO consistently.

You may not need one yet if your business gets all its work from referrals, if you can spend about five hours a week on SEO yourself, or if your website has basic problems that need a rebuild first. In that case, start with our local SEO checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-checklist/) and the free SEO audit tool (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/seo-audit-tool/).

### Is SEO worth it?

For most businesses that customers search for, yes, because organic visibility keeps producing calls without paying for each click. The return depends on three things: how many people search for your services, how much a new customer is worth, and how competitive your market is. A plumber or dentist in a mid-size city usually needs only a few extra jobs or patients a month to cover a local SEO plan. SEO is a poor fit when nobody searches for what you sell or when you need results within weeks; paid ads suit that better.

### How much SEO services cost

Most small businesses pay between $500 and $2,500 a month for ongoing SEO, with one-time audits and projects priced separately. RankEmpire publishes its prices: local plans start at $599 a month, with no long contracts. See how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) for a full breakdown and our SEO packages (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/) for what each plan includes.


### Sources

- Google Search Central: Do you need an SEO? (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo)

### FAQ

#### What does an SEO company do?

An SEO company improves a business's visibility in search engines and AI answers. It fixes technical problems, builds and improves pages that match customer searches, optimizes the Google Business Profile, earns reviews and links, and reports results from Search Console and lead data.

#### What is an SEO agency?

An SEO agency is a team of specialists that handles search engine optimization for other businesses: strategy, technical SEO, content, local SEO and link building. "SEO agency" and "SEO company" usually mean the same thing.

#### What are SEO services?

SEO services are the tasks that improve how a website ranks in search: technical fixes, keyword and content work, on-page optimization, local SEO, link building and reporting. Agencies sell them as monthly plans or one-time projects such as audits.

#### Do I need an SEO company or can I do SEO myself?

You can do the basics yourself with a few hours a week and good guides. An SEO company makes sense when your market is competitive, when nobody has time to work on SEO consistently, or when technical problems need a specialist.

#### How long before an SEO company shows results?

Early gains on low-competition searches often appear within four to eight weeks. Competitive terms usually take four to six months. Impressions in Search Console rise first, then positions, then clicks and leads.

#### What does an SEO consultant do?

An SEO consultant audits a site, sets strategy and advises a business or its team on what to change. Unlike a full-service agency, a consultant often leaves most of the implementation to the client's team.


## SEO Keywords by Industry: Keyword Lists for 16 Local Businesses
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/seo-keywords-by-industry/
Updated: 2026-11-14

The best SEO keywords for a local business are the exact phrases customers type when they are ready to hire: the service, the problem, the price question and the place. This guide gives starter keyword lists for 16 local industries, grouped by search intent, and shows how to turn each group into the right page. Use them as seeds, then confirm which ones already show your site in Google Search Console.

### How to use these keyword lists

Every list below is split into five groups, because each group belongs on a different kind of page:

| Group | What it signals | Where it belongs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service keywords | Ready to hire for a specific job | One service page per job |
| Urgent keywords | Needs help now | Emergency page and Google Business Profile |
| Cost keywords | Comparing options | Pricing section or a cost guide |
| Local keywords | Wants someone nearby | Location and service area pages |
| Question keywords | Researching | FAQs and blog guides |

Add your city or neighborhood to service and urgent keywords ("water heater repair Katy"). Google treats "near me" searches by location automatically, so you rarely need to write "near me" on the page; you need accurate service areas and a strong Google Business Profile (https://www.rankempire.us/google-business-profile-seo/).

### Plumbing keywords

- **Service:** water heater repair, water heater installation, tankless water heater installation, drain cleaning, sewer line repair, sewer camera inspection, leak detection, repiping, toilet repair, garbage disposal installation
- **Urgent:** emergency plumber, 24 hour plumber, burst pipe repair, clogged drain, sewer backup, no hot water
- **Cost:** water heater replacement cost, sewer line replacement cost, cost to repipe a house
- **Local:** plumber [city], plumbing company [city], best plumber [neighborhood]
- **Questions:** why is my water heater leaking, how long does a water heater last, what causes low water pressure

See the full SEO for plumbers (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-plumbers/) playbook.

### HVAC keywords

- **Service:** AC repair, AC installation, furnace repair, furnace replacement, heat pump installation, ductless mini split installation, HVAC maintenance, duct cleaning, thermostat installation
- **Urgent:** emergency AC repair, AC not cooling, furnace not working, 24 hour HVAC repair
- **Cost:** AC replacement cost, new furnace cost, heat pump cost, HVAC maintenance plan price
- **Local:** HVAC company [city], AC repair [city], heating and cooling [city]
- **Questions:** why is my AC blowing warm air, how often should I replace my air filter, heat pump vs furnace

See HVAC SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-hvac/).

### Electrician keywords

- **Service:** panel upgrade, EV charger installation, whole house rewiring, outlet installation, lighting installation, generator installation, electrical inspection, ceiling fan installation
- **Urgent:** emergency electrician, power outage repair, breaker keeps tripping, burning smell from outlet
- **Cost:** panel upgrade cost, EV charger installation cost, cost to rewire a house
- **Local:** electrician [city], licensed electrician [city], electrical contractor [city]
- **Questions:** do I need a permit for an EV charger, how long does a panel upgrade take, what size panel do I need

See electrician SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-electricians/).

### Roofing keywords

- **Service:** roof repair, roof replacement, metal roofing, shingle roof installation, flat roof repair, roof inspection, gutter installation
- **Urgent:** emergency roof repair, roof leak repair, storm damage roof repair, hail damage roof inspection
- **Cost:** roof replacement cost, metal roof cost, roof repair cost
- **Local:** roofing company [city], roofer [city], roofing contractor [city]
- **Questions:** does insurance cover roof replacement, how long does a roof last, metal vs shingle roof

See roofing SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-roofing/).

### Dental keywords

- **Service:** dental implants, Invisalign, teeth whitening, root canal, dental crowns, veneers, teeth cleaning, pediatric dentist
- **Urgent:** emergency dentist, same day dentist, tooth pain, broken tooth repair
- **Cost:** dental implant cost, Invisalign cost, root canal cost, veneers cost
- **Local:** dentist [city], family dentist [neighborhood], cosmetic dentist [city]
- **Questions:** are dental implants painful, how long does Invisalign take, implant vs bridge

See dental SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-dentists/) and orthodontist SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-orthodontists/).

### Law firm keywords

- **Urgent:** arrested what to do, lawyer free consultation, DUI lawyer near me

- **Questions:** how long does a divorce take, do I need a lawyer for a will, what to do after a car accident

### Turn keywords into pages

1. **Pick one primary keyword per page.** Put it at the start of the title, in the H1 and in the first sentence.
2. **Use close variants as secondary keywords.** "Water heater repair", "water heater replacement" and "fix water heater" can share one page.
3. **Answer the questions on the page.** Add a short FAQ with the question keywords and direct answers; it helps featured snippets and AI answers, as explained in AEO vs GEO vs SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo/).
4. **Check real demand.** Search Console shows which searches already show your site. Generate more ideas with our free keyword research tool (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/keyword-research-tool/) and check where you rank with the keyword rank checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/).
5. **Build local pages carefully.** Only create a city page where you have real work and reviews there. Our SEO for contractors (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/seo-for-contractors/) guide covers how.

### FAQ

#### What are the best SEO keywords for a local business?

The best keywords combine a specific service with a location or an urgent need, such as "emergency plumber Houston" or "ceramic coating Scottsdale". They have lower search volume than broad terms but far higher intent, and they are easier to rank for.

#### Should I put "near me" in my keywords?

Usually not on the page itself. Google interprets "near me" using the searcher's location and your Google Business Profile, service areas and reviews. Focus on accurate location details and pages for the areas you serve.

#### How many keywords should one page target?

One primary keyword and a handful of close variants with the same intent. If two keywords need different answers, they need different pages.

#### How do I find which keywords my site already ranks for?

Open Google Search Console, go to Performance and look at the Queries tab. It lists every search that showed your site, with impressions and average position. Pages at positions 11 to 30 are the quickest wins.

#### Do I need a paid keyword tool?

Not to start. Search Console, Google's autocomplete, People Also Ask boxes and your own customer calls give plenty of keywords. Paid tools add search volume and difficulty data, which helps when choosing between many options.


## How We Got 123 of 124 Pages Indexed: A Real Search Console Case Study
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-we-got-our-pages-indexed/
Updated: 2026-11-06

RankEmpire went from 17 indexed pages to 123 of 124, and from 6 Google impressions a day to 2,021 a day in eight days. This case study shows exactly what we changed, in the order we changed it, with the real numbers from our own Google Search Console. Nothing here is a mockup or an estimate, and the parts that have not worked yet are included too.

!Line chart of daily Google impressions for rankempire.us rising from 6 on 27 October to 2,021 on 3 November 2026 (https://www.rankempire.us/img/b-indexing-case.webp "Daily impressions from Google Search Console, 27 October to 3 November 2026")

### The starting point

The site launched with 124 pages: service pages, 51 industry pages, 17 city pages, free SEO tools and a blog. Google had indexed 17 of them. The rest sat in Search Console as "Discovered, currently not indexed" or "Crawled, currently not indexed", which is the most common state for a new site with little authority.

:::kt
17 → 123|Pages indexed out of 124
6 → 2,021|Daily Google impressions, 27 Oct to 3 Nov
8,334|Impressions in the last 28 days
:::

### Step 1: Fix what tells Google a page is low value

Before asking Google to crawl more, we removed the reasons it might skip a page:

- **Doubled brand names in titles.** A layout template added "| RankEmpire" to titles that already ended with it. We switched every page to an absolute title.
- **Near-duplicate sections.** Several service pages shared the same intro blocks. The one page that stayed unindexed longest, International SEO, was fixed by giving it a distinct long-form guide and more internal links.
- **Price contradictions.** Some pages said local plans start at $799 while the pricing card on the same page said $599. We made every mention consistent.

### Step 2: Split the sitemap and keep dates honest

One large sitemap became a sitemap index with four children: core pages (36), industries (51), locations (17) and content (20). Each URL carries a real last-modified date that changes only when the page changes. Split sitemaps make it obvious in Search Console which group is lagging, and honest dates give Google a reason to recrawl what actually changed.

### Step 3: Build internal links like a hub and spoke

Orphan and weakly linked pages are the first ones Google ignores. We generated a related-links block for 92 pages: every industry page links to related industries, two cities and two guides; every city links to nearby cities; every service links to sibling services and posts. Blog posts link to the industry and city pages they mention. The weakest pages went from 3 internal links to 5 or more.

### Step 4: Give every page something worth indexing

Thin pages rarely get indexed. We added three things to the pages with impressions:

1. **A direct answer block** near the top, answering the question the page targets in two or three sentences.
2. **A long-form guide** written for the exact searches Search Console showed for that page.
3. **Real proof**, linking to verified Search Console reports on our case studies (https://www.rankempire.us/case-studies/) page.

### Step 5: Structured data on every page

Every page now carries Organization data, a breadcrumb trail and, where relevant, Service, FAQPage, BlogPosting or WebApplication markup. Our checker reports zero errors across all pages. Structured data does not force indexing, but it removes ambiguity about what each page is.

### Step 6: Submit, inspect and request

We resubmitted the sitemaps, ran URL Inspection on every route to find what was still excluded, and sent all 124 URLs through Google's Indexing API, plus IndexNow for Bing. Indexing moved from 17 pages to 123 of 124 in the weeks that followed, and impressions climbed from 6 to 2,021 a day within eight days of the push.

### What has not worked yet

Impressions are not clicks. Over the last 28 days the site earned 8,334 impressions and 2 clicks, at an average position of 84. Google now knows what every page is about, but it does not yet trust the site enough to rank it on page one. That trust comes from links and mentions on other sites, which no amount of on-page work replaces. Our next phase is earning those links, as described in our link building (https://www.rankempire.us/link-building/) approach.

### What to copy for your own site

- Check Search Console's Pages report first and fix duplicates and thin pages before submitting anything.
- Split large sitemaps by page type and keep last-modified dates honest.
- Make sure every important page has at least five internal links from relevant pages.
- Add a direct answer, specific details and real proof to each page you want indexed.
- Validate structured data with a schema checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/schema-checker/) and a sitemap checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/sitemap-checker/).
- Expect impressions to move weeks before clicks.

If your pages are stuck in "Discovered, currently not indexed", our free SEO audit (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-audit/) includes the same indexing review we ran here.

### FAQ

#### How long does it take Google to index a new website?

Small, well-linked sites are often indexed within days. Larger new sites with little authority can wait weeks or months for most pages. Fixing duplicates, internal links and sitemaps, then requesting indexing, usually shortens that from months to weeks.

#### Why are my pages "Discovered, currently not indexed"?

Google found the URL but decided crawling it was not worth the effort yet. Common causes are low site authority, thin or duplicated content, weak internal linking and too many similar pages. Improve those, then resubmit the sitemap.

#### Does the Google Indexing API work for normal pages?

Google officially supports it only for job postings and livestream pages. It often speeds up crawling for other pages, but it does not guarantee indexing or rankings. Fixing page quality and internal links matters more.

#### Why do I have impressions but no clicks?

Impressions at positions 50 to 100 mean Google shows your page deep in the results, where almost nobody scrolls. Clicks start when pages reach the first page, which usually requires links and mentions from other sites on top of good on-page SEO.


## SEO for Contractors: How Home Service Businesses Win Google Maps and AI Search
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/seo-for-contractors/
Updated: 2026-11-12

SEO for contractors comes down to three things: winning the Google Maps pack in the towns you serve, having one strong page for every job you want more of, and earning reviews that mention the job and the town. This guide covers how plumbers, electricians, roofers, HVAC companies, painters and other home service contractors rank in Google and in AI answers, and links to the detailed playbook for each trade.

### Why contractor SEO is different

Most contractor searches are local and urgent. "Water heater repair near me", "roof leak repair Katy" or "electrician open now" are decided in minutes, usually from the map pack on a phone. That makes contractor SEO closer to local SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/local-seo/) than to national content marketing. The website still matters, because Google reads it to decide which jobs you do and where, but the Google Business Profile, reviews and service area signals decide most of the calls.

AI assistants now add a second path. ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI Overviews answer questions like "best roofer in Plano for hail damage" by reading the same profiles, reviews and service pages. Contractors with clear, specific information get named; vague ones get skipped, as we explain in AEO vs GEO vs SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo/).

### 1. Set up the Google Business Profile for the job, not the company

Choose the most specific primary category, such as Plumber, Electrician, Roofing Contractor or HVAC Contractor, then add secondary categories only for work you actually do. List every service with a short description, set realistic service areas, keep hours accurate (including emergency hours) and upload real job photos every month. Our Google Business Profile checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) walks through every field.

For starter keyword lists by trade, see our guide to SEO keywords by industry (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/seo-keywords-by-industry/).

### 2. Build one page per high-value job

A single "Services" page cannot rank for water heaters, sewer lines, panel upgrades and roof replacements at the same time. Each job you want more of needs its own page with:

- What the job involves and how long it takes
- Price ranges or starting prices, with what changes the price
- Brands, materials or equipment you work with
- Photos from real projects
- Licensing, insurance and warranty details
- A short FAQ using the questions customers ask on the phone

Starting prices matter more than most contractors expect. Customers and AI assistants both compare, and a page that says "water heater replacement from $1,450 installed" is easier to recommend than "call for a quote".

### 3. Add service area pages only where you really work

Pages for each town you serve can rank well, but only with real local detail: jobs completed there, local permit or code notes, reviews from customers in that town and the services offered there. Pages that only swap the city name rarely rank and can drag down the whole site.

### 4. Turn reviews into ranking signals

Reviews are one of the strongest local ranking factors you control. Ask every customer, by text, within a day of the job, and ask them to mention the job and the town: "they replaced our water heater in Sugar Land the same day" helps far more than "great service". Reply to every review, good or bad.

### 5. Use the right structured data

Mark up the site with LocalBusiness data using the most specific type schema.org offers, such as Plumber, Electrician, HVACBusiness, RoofingContractor or GeneralContractor, plus Service markup for each job page and FAQ markup where the questions are unique. Check it with our free schema checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/schema-checker/).

### 6. Earn local links

The best links for contractors are local and real: suppliers and manufacturers' dealer locators, trade associations, the chamber of commerce, local news coverage of a project, sponsorships of youth teams and partner businesses such as realtors and property managers. A handful of these beats hundreds of directory links.

### 7. Plan for seasons

Contractor demand is seasonal: AC repair in early summer, furnaces in fall, roofing after storms, pools in spring. Publish and update seasonal pages two to three months before demand peaks, so they are indexed and ranking when customers start searching.

### Regional SEO for contractors serving several cities

Many contractors cover a whole region rather than one town: a roofer serving three counties, or an HVAC company covering a metro and its suburbs. Regional SEO works in layers:

1. **One Google Business Profile per real location.** A profile needs a genuine address or a service area tied to a real base. Adding fake offices to reach more towns risks suspension.
2. **Service area pages for the towns that bring revenue.** Each page needs proof of work there: projects, photos, reviews and local details such as permits or common housing types.
3. **A regional hub page.** One page that lists every town you serve, links to each service area page and explains how far you travel and any trip fees.
4. **Reviews from across the region.** Ask customers in outlying towns to mention their town; those reviews help you rank beyond your office's immediate area.
5. **Rank grids per area.** Measure visibility separately in each part of your region, because map results change every few miles.

### Playbooks by trade

Each trade has its own searches, seasons and conversion paths. These pages cover the details:

| Trade | Playbook |
| --- | --- |
| Plumbers | SEO for plumbers (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-plumbers/) |
| Electricians | Electrician SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-electricians/) |
| HVAC | HVAC SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-hvac/) |
| Roofers | Roofing SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-roofing/) |

| Home builders | SEO for home builders (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-home-builders/) |

### How long contractor SEO takes

Profile fixes and reviews often show results in the map pack within 30 to 60 days. New job pages and service area pages usually take three to six months to rank for competitive terms, faster in smaller towns. Our 90-day local SEO roadmap (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/) shows the order we work in, and how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) covers typical budgets.

### FAQ

#### What is the most important SEO factor for contractors?

For most contractors it is the Google Business Profile: the right primary category, accurate service areas, steady reviews that mention the job and town, and regular photos. The website supports it with one strong page per job.

#### Should contractors publish prices on their website?

Publishing starting prices or ranges usually helps. Customers and AI assistants compare options, and specific numbers make a contractor easier to choose. You can explain what changes the final price without committing to a fixed quote.

#### What is local SEO for contractors?

Local SEO for contractors is the work that puts a trade business in Google Maps and the local results for searches in its service area: a complete Google Business Profile, one page per service, pages for the towns you serve, steady reviews and local links.

#### Do contractors need a page for every city they serve?

Only for towns where you have real work, reviews and something specific to say. A few strong service area pages outperform dozens of near-identical ones.

#### Is SEO or Google Local Services Ads better for contractors?

They work together. Local Services Ads buy immediate visibility for a fee per lead, while SEO builds rankings that keep producing calls without paying per click. Many contractors use ads while their organic rankings grow.

#### How much does SEO cost for a contractor?

Single-location local plans at RankEmpire start at $599 a month. Multi-location and competitive metro programs cost more. See our SEO packages (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/) for what each plan includes.


## What Is AI Agent Optimization (AGO)? How to Get Chosen When AI Books and Buys
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/ai-agent-optimization/
Updated: 2026-11-02

For twenty years, getting found meant ranking on a page a person would read. That is changing. AI assistants now take actions as well as answer questions. ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and the assistants built into phones and browsers can compare providers, check availability, fill in a quote form and book an appointment on a user's behalf. When an AI agent makes the shortlist, the user may never see a search results page or your homepage.

AI agent optimization (AGO) is the work of making your business the one those agents can understand, trust and transact with. This guide explains what AGO is, how it differs from SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-services/), AEO (https://www.rankempire.us/aeo/) and GEO (https://www.rankempire.us/geo/), what agents actually look at, and the 10-step checklist we use to make a business agent-ready.

### What AI agent optimization means

AI agent optimization is the practice of structuring a business's data, website and booking flows so that AI agents acting for a user can find it, verify it and complete a task with it: request a quote, check a price, book a slot or buy a product.

It sits one step past generative engine optimization. GEO gets your brand named in an AI answer. AGO gets your business chosen and used when the assistant moves from answering to doing.

| | SEO | AEO | GEO | AGO |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The user | Reads results and clicks | Reads one quoted answer | Reads an AI summary | Delegates the task |
| Who decides | The person | The person, guided by the snippet | The person, guided by the AI | The agent, within the person's rules |
| What wins | Relevant, authoritative pages | Quotable passages | Trusted, cited sources | Verifiable data and a completable action |
| Failure looks like | Page four | Someone else's snippet | Not mentioned | Agent skips you because it cannot confirm price, availability or how to book |

The important row is the last one. An agent that cannot confirm what you charge, when you are open, what area you serve or how to book will usually move on to a competitor whose information is clear. Agents are cautious by design, because a wrong booking is worse than no booking.

### How AI agents choose a business

Agents are still young and every platform works a little differently, but the pattern is consistent. An agent given a task such as "book a plumber for tomorrow morning" or "find three limo companies for a wedding on June 14 and get quotes" goes through roughly four stages:

1. **Discovery.** It searches the web and the platforms it trusts: Google and Bing results, Google Business Profile and Apple Maps data, review sites and industry marketplaces. Classic local SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/local-seo/) still decides who is in this pool.
2. **Verification.** It checks that the business is real and fits the constraints: location and service area, hours, services offered, price range, ratings, licensing. Inconsistent data between your site and your listings is the most common reason a business drops out here.
3. **Comparison.** It ranks the shortlist against the user's criteria, usually price, availability, reviews and distance. Specific numbers beat vague claims every time.
4. **Action.** It tries to complete the task: a booking widget, a quote form, an email or a phone call through a voice agent. A form that needs a human to solve a puzzle, a booking flow hidden behind a sales call, or a phone line nobody answers ends the attempt.

Every stage favors businesses whose information is structured, consistent and machine-readable.

### What agents look for

#### Structured business data

The single most useful thing you can give an agent is clean, structured data about the business. That means LocalBusiness or Organization schema on your site with the same name, address, phone, hours, service area and price range that appear on your Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places and Yelp. Add Service schema for each service and Offer or Product schema where you sell defined packages with prices. Validate it with our free schema checker (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-tools/schema-checker/); broken markup is worse than none because it signals an unreliable source.

#### Prices, availability and terms in plain text

Agents compare. If your price is "call for a quote" and a competitor publishes "airport transfers from $95, two-hour minimum for weddings", the competitor is far easier to recommend. You do not need to publish every price, but published starting prices, minimums, deposits and cancellation terms make you comparable. Our guide on how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) is an example of the format: ranges, what drives the price and what is included.

#### A path to complete the task

Agents need a way to act. In order of how well they work today:

- An online booking or scheduling system with real availability.
- A short quote or contact form with clear required fields and no friction beyond basic spam protection.
- A published email address that someone answers.
- A phone line that is answered, since voice agents increasingly place calls.

The best businesses offer the first two and make sure the confirmation goes somewhere a human will see within hours.

#### Consistent listings everywhere agents look

Your website is only one source. Agents cross-check Google Business Profile, Apple Maps, Bing, Yelp, industry marketplaces and review sites. Identical names, categories, hours and service areas across all of them are what verification depends on. Our Google Business Profile checklist (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) covers the most important listing in detail.

#### Reviews with specifics

Agents read reviews to judge fit, not just star ratings. Reviews that mention the service, the area and the outcome ("they fixed our water heater in Katy the same afternoon") help an agent match you to a request. A steady flow of specific reviews is one of the strongest signals you control.

#### Open access for AI crawlers

Assistants can only use what they can read. Allow GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and similar crawlers in robots.txt, keep key information in HTML rather than images or PDFs, and consider publishing an llms.txt file that summarizes your business, services and key pages. This site publishes one (https://www.rankempire.us/llms.txt) for that reason.

### Which businesses need AGO first

Any business where the customer's task can be delegated benefits, but some are already seeing agent-driven inquiries:

- **Local services with urgent, simple jobs:** plumbers, electricians, locksmiths, towing and cleaning. "Find someone who can come today" is an ideal agent task. See our playbooks for plumbers (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-plumbers/) and electricians (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-electricians/).
- **Bookings with clear criteria:** restaurants, salons, gyms and clinics, where date, time and party size define the request.
- **Transportation and rentals:** limousine companies (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-limousine-companies/), exotic car rentals (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-exotic-car-rental/), yacht charters (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-yacht-charter/) and private jet charters (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-private-jet-charter/), where travelers and assistants compare price, capacity and availability for specific dates.
- **Events and venues:** wedding venues and event companies (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-wedding-venues/), where capacity, dates and package pricing drive the shortlist.
- **E-commerce:** stores with clean product data, prices, stock and shipping terms, which shopping agents can compare and buy from.

### The 10-step agent-readiness checklist

1. **Audit your data consistency.** Compare name, address, phone, hours, categories and service area across your site, Google, Apple, Bing, Yelp and your top industry directories. Fix every mismatch.
2. **Add complete structured data.** LocalBusiness or Organization, Service for each service, Offer or Product with prices, FAQPage where the questions are unique, and sameAs links to your official profiles.
3. **Publish prices or starting prices.** Plus minimums, deposits and what is included. Agents compare; give them something to compare.
4. **State availability clearly.** Hours, lead times, booking windows and seasonal limits in plain text on the relevant pages.
5. **Make booking and quoting completable.** One short form or a real booking system, with a confirmation that reaches a person quickly.
6. **Answer the phone and the inbox.** Voice and email agents are already contacting businesses. Slow or missing responses lose the booking.
7. **Write terms in plain language.** Cancellation, refunds, insurance and requirements on a page agents can read and quote.
8. **Collect specific reviews.** Ask customers to mention the service and location. Reply to every review.
9. **Open the door to AI crawlers.** Check robots.txt, keep content in HTML and publish an llms.txt summary.
10. **Test it yourself.** Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity to find, compare and book a business like yours in your area. Note who they pick, what data they cite and where your business falls out. Repeat monthly.

### How AGO fits with SEO, AEO and GEO

AGO is not a separate program. Most of the work overlaps: technical health, consistent entity data, structured content and authority serve all four surfaces. That is why RankEmpire runs them together, as explained in our guide to AEO vs GEO vs SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo/). The AGO-specific layer is the transaction side: prices, availability, terms and a path an agent can complete.

If you want to know how agent-ready your business is today, our free audit (https://www.rankempire.us/contact-us/) includes a structured data and listing consistency check alongside the classic SEO review, and every SEO plan (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/) includes the entity and schema work that AGO depends on.

### FAQ

#### What is AI agent optimization (AGO)?

AI agent optimization is the practice of making a business easy for AI agents to find, verify and transact with when they act on a user's behalf. It focuses on structured business data, consistent listings, published prices and availability, and booking or quote flows an agent can complete.

#### How is AGO different from GEO?

Generative engine optimization gets your brand mentioned and cited in AI answers. AI agent optimization goes a step further and makes your business usable when the assistant takes an action, such as comparing quotes or booking an appointment. GEO earns the mention; AGO earns the transaction.

#### Do AI agents really book appointments today?

Yes, in growing numbers. Assistants can already search, compare, fill in forms and place calls for some tasks, and booking and shopping features are expanding across the major AI platforms. Businesses with clean data and simple booking flows are the ones agents can use reliably.

#### What is the quickest AGO win for a local business?

Make your business data identical across your website and every major listing, add LocalBusiness schema with your hours, service area and price range, and publish starting prices with a simple booking or quote form. Those three steps remove most of the reasons an agent would skip you.

#### Does AGO replace SEO?

No. Agents discover businesses through the same search indexes and listings that SEO and local SEO improve. AGO builds on that foundation by making the business verifiable and actionable once it is found.

#### How do I measure AI agent optimization?

Track structured data coverage and listing accuracy, run a monthly set of agent-style prompts across the main assistants to see whether your business is chosen, and tag bookings and inquiries that arrive through AI assistants or voice calls.


## How to Find and Choose the Best SEO Company: 12 Questions to Ask
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/
Updated: 2026-11-17

Finding the best SEO company for your business starts with knowing what to ask. Choosing an SEO company is hard because most of the work is invisible until months later. Two agencies can send near-identical proposals at very different prices, and the difference only shows up in month six, when one has built rankings that compound and the other has a report full of activity and a flat graph. This guide gives you the twelve questions that separate them, the red flags to walk away from, and a simple way to compare proposals side by side, whether you are hiring an SEO company in New York (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/new-york/), a Chicago SEO agency (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/chicago/) or a specialist for your industry.

### Start with what you need, not who is selling

Before talking to any agency, write down three things. They make every conversation sharper and every proposal easier to compare.

- **The outcome.** More calls from the map pack, more online sales, more demo requests, or more qualified leads from a specific city. "More traffic" is not an outcome.
- **The scope.** One location or many, one service or twenty, a local market or the whole country.
- **The budget range and timeline.** A realistic monthly figure and how long you can commit before judging results. Our guide on how much SEO costs (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) gives ranges by business type.

With those three written down, you can tell quickly whether an agency is proposing to solve your problem or selling its standard package.

### The 12 questions to ask every SEO company

#### 1. What will you do in the first 90 days, in order?

A credible agency describes a sequence: audit, technical fixes, foundations, then content and authority. If the answer starts with "we will write four blog posts a month", the order is wrong. Our 90-day local SEO roadmap (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/) is an example of what a real sequence looks like.

#### 2. What exactly is delivered each month?

Ask for deliverables you can count: pages built or rewritten, technical issues fixed, links earned, profile updates, reports. "Ongoing optimization" is not a deliverable.

#### 3. Who does the work, and who do I talk to?

Find out whether a strategist does the work or an account manager relays messages to an outsourced team. At RankEmpire every account has one senior strategist who does the work and takes the calls, led by founder Gaurav Kapoor; ask any agency you consider to name the person.

#### 4. How do you earn links?

Good answers: outreach, digital PR, partnerships, original data, content worth citing. Bad answers: "our network", "guest post packages", "100 links a month". Link schemes are the fastest way to lose rankings, as covered in why most SEO campaigns fail (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/why-most-seo-campaigns-fail/).

#### 5. Can I see real results?

Ask for Search Console screenshots from real clients, shared with permission, not rank tracker charts or mockups. Clicks and impressions from Google's own data are hard to fake. Our case studies (https://www.rankempire.us/case-studies/) are all real Search Console reports for this reason.

#### 6. How will you report, and what will you measure?

Rankings and traffic are fine as leading indicators, but the report should connect to calls, forms, bookings and revenue. Ask to see a sample report.

#### 7. What is the contract?

Month to month after a short onboarding period is fair. A twelve-month lock-in with no exit clause protects the agency, not you.

#### 8. Who owns the work if we stop?

You should own every page, piece of content, account and profile created for you. Some agencies keep content on their own domains or hold your Google Business Profile hostage. Get ownership in writing.

#### 9. What do you need from us?

Good SEO needs access (site, Search Console, analytics, Business Profile) and some of your time for approvals and expertise. An agency that asks for nothing will produce generic work.

#### 10. How do you handle AI search?

Search now includes featured snippets, AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity answers, and AI agents that compare and book. Ask how the agency covers answer engine (https://www.rankempire.us/aeo/), generative engine (https://www.rankempire.us/geo/) and AI agent optimization (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/ai-agent-optimization/), not just the classic results.

#### 11. Have you worked in my industry or market?

Industry experience shortens the learning curve: an agency that has run SEO for electricians (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-electricians/) knows emergency searches and permit content; one that has done auto detailing SEO (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-for-auto-detailing/) knows that model-level and package pages drive bookings. Ask for the specific playbook, not a logo slide.

#### 12. What will you not do?

Good agencies turn down work that will not pay back and tell you when SEO is the wrong channel. If every answer is yes, be careful.

### Red flags that mean walk away

- **Guaranteed rankings.** Nobody controls Google. A guarantee of position one means either a meaningless keyword or a risky tactic.
- **Results in 30 days.** Real SEO takes three to six months to compound. Fast promises usually mean paid links or spam.
- **Secret methods.** "Proprietary techniques we cannot share" usually hide something you would not approve.
- **Huge link counts.** Hundreds of links a month at a low price are almost always low quality.
- **No access for you.** If you cannot see your own Search Console, analytics or Business Profile, you cannot verify anything.
- **Long lock-ins.** Twelve or twenty-four months with no exit is a sign the agency does not expect you to stay voluntarily.
- **Reports with only rankings.** Positions for obscure keywords are easy to show and do not pay bills.

### How to compare proposals side by side

Put each proposal into the same five rows and the right choice usually becomes obvious:

| Compare | What good looks like |
| --- | --- |
| First 90 days | A clear sequence starting with an audit and technical fixes |
| Monthly deliverables | Countable outputs: pages, fixes, links, profile work |
| People | A named strategist who does the work |
| Measurement | Calls, leads and revenue next to rankings and traffic |
| Terms | Month to month after onboarding, you own everything |

Price comes last. A cheaper proposal that fails three rows costs more in the end than a fair one that passes all five.

### Local agency or remote specialist?

A local agency knows your city's neighborhoods and competition, and some businesses value meeting in person. A remote specialist may know your industry better and often costs less because overheads are lower. What matters more than location is whether the team understands your market. For local businesses, ask any agency, local or not, to show how they would rank you across your whole service area, not just near your office; that is what a rank grid report is for. RankEmpire works remotely with US businesses and runs dedicated programs in cities like Houston (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/houston/), Los Angeles (https://www.rankempire.us/locations/los-angeles/), New York and Chicago.

### When SEO consulting is the better choice

If you have an in-house marketer or developer, you may not need a full-service agency. SEO consulting (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-consulting/) gives your team the strategy, audits and reviews while they do the work, usually at a lower monthly cost. It works best when someone internal has the time and the access to ship changes.


New to hiring SEO help? Start with what an SEO company does (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/what-does-an-seo-company-do/). If you are comparing "best SEO company" lists, read who is the best SEO company in the USA (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/best-seo-company-in-the-usa/) and, for map rankings, who is the best local SEO company (https://www.rankempire.us/blog/who-is-the-best-local-seo-company/).


### Sources

- Google Search Central: Do you need an SEO? (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo)

### FAQ

#### How do I know if an SEO company is legitimate?

Check for real Search Console results shared with permission, a named strategist, clear monthly deliverables, transparent link building methods and fair contract terms. Avoid any company that guarantees rankings or results in 30 days.

#### How much should I pay an SEO company?

Most small businesses pay $500 to $2,500 a month, multi-location and e-commerce programs $2,000 to $8,000, and national or enterprise programs more. The right price funds the full sequence of work rather than a piece of it. See our pricing (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/) for exact plans.

#### How long before an SEO company shows results?

Expect early movement on low-competition and branded searches within four to eight weeks, meaningful gains for core terms in four to six months, and compounding growth after that. Leading indicators like impressions and positions should move first.

#### Should I sign a long-term SEO contract?

A short onboarding period of around three months is reasonable because early work is front-loaded. After that, month to month with 30 days notice is fair and keeps the agency accountable.

#### What should an SEO company report every month?

Work completed, rankings and visibility for target searches, organic traffic, and the business results that matter: calls, form submissions, bookings and revenue from organic search, plus what comes next.

#### Is it better to hire an SEO company or a freelancer?

Freelancers can be excellent for focused tasks and smaller budgets. Agencies make sense when you need several skills at once, such as technical SEO, content, links and local work, or continuity if one person is unavailable.


## How Much Does SEO Cost in 2026? Real Prices, What You Get and How to Compare
URL: https://www.rankempire.us/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/
Updated: 2026-11-18

"How much does SEO cost?" is the first question on almost every call we take, and the honest answer is a range with reasons behind it. This guide gives you the ranges we see in the US market in 2026, what each price level actually buys, the questions that separate a fair quote from a bad one, and how to judge whether SEO is worth it for your business at all. Where we quote RankEmpire's own numbers, they are the ones on our SEO packages page (https://www.rankempire.us/seo-packages/), so you can check them.

### The short answer

:::kt
$500 to $1,500 / month|Local SEO for a single-location service business, run by a small agency or specialist
$1,500 to $5,000 / month|Multi-location local, regional, small e-commerce or SaaS programs with content and links
$5,000 to $20,000+ / month|National, enterprise and competitive e-commerce or SaaS programs with dedicated teams
:::
